summary: P2 Admin Orders Operational Dashboard frontend verification: page loads cleanly (no lucide icon crash), dashboard renders with all 9 count cards + 5-tile revenue row, lifecycle-stage badge + 3-chip row render per order, expanding a PAID order shows ownership-panel + all 4 P1 controls, and the Mark Refunded -> Reinstate Paid round-trip on order SF-2026-GVQVV worked end-to-end. State was successfully REVERTED — final dashboard back to Refunded=0, Net=$113.77, GVQVV stage=CLOSED. Net = Gross - Refunds invariant holds ($113.77 = $113.77 - $0.00). All non-negative. Physical Fulfillment panel did not appear (expected — dataset is all digital, per main agent context).

ui_bugs.issue: After clicking Mark Refunded / Reinstate Paid (and likely Mark Cancelled / Revoke / Reinstate Access etc.), the per-order chips and lifecycle stage update inline (good), but the top dashboard summary cards (Refunded, Completed, Closed) and revenue row (Refunds $, Net $) do NOT refresh — they keep showing pre-action values until a full page reload or the next polling tick. Observed: Refunded=0/Refunds=$0 before refund -> still 0/$0 immediately after click; only after navigating away and back did counts catch up. Root cause: action handlers in AdminOrders.js only call fetchOrders() and never fetchSummary(). Add fetchSummary() alongside every fetchOrders() in markRefunded / markCancelled / reinstatePaid / revokeAccess / refund / etc. handlers.

Console emits a steady stream of React 'Encountered two children with the same key' warnings on every render of the orders list (~14 per render cycle, fires repeatedly). Some list .map() in AdminOrders.js (likely chips array, refund-requests, or items) is using a non-unique key. Not breaking but pollutes the console and risks future render bugs.

action_items: AdminOrders.js: call fetchSummary() in addition to fetchOrders() in every action handler (markRefunded, reinstatePaid, markCancelled, revokeAccess, refund handler, sync-stripe, mark-paid, refulfill, grant-access, etc.) so the operational dashboard counts and revenue stay live with each click — currently only the polling/initial-mount triggers fetchSummary.

AdminOrders.js: find the .map() emitting duplicate keys (probably the lifecycle chips array or refundRequests/items list) and switch the key to a stable unique value (e.g. `${order.order_number}-${chipName}` or refund-request id).
critical_code_review_comments: Action handlers desynchronize the operational dashboard from per-row state — fetchSummary() must be paired with fetchOrders() in every mutating handler. Otherwise the 'at-a-glance' dashboard misrepresents the state immediately after any admin action, which defeats the purpose of P2.
Duplicate React key warnings on the orders list should be fixed before adding more dynamic per-row features; non-unique keys can cause chips/badges to appear on the wrong row during reorder/refetch.

Visibility filter dropdown returned the same Total (71) for both 'active' and 'all' — likely correct given current dataset has no archived/test-only orders, but worth seeding 1 archived order to fully prove the filter narrows results.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing order SF-2026-GVQVV (CLOSED/PAID) for Refund->Reinstate round-trip; FULLY REVERTED to original CLOSED/paid/granted/downloaded state.
context_for_next_testing_agent: P2 dashboard, lifecycle stage badge, 3-chip rows, ownership panel, and P1 refund/reinstate controls all functional. Physical Fulfillment panel was NOT exercised because the dataset is 100% digital — backend lifecycle for physical was verified by the main agent via DB script. If you need to UI-test the fulfillment panel (mark-packed/shipped/delivered, tracking-input, carrier-input, notify-checkbox), you must first seed a physical-bearing order in DB. GVQVV is back to clean CLOSED state.
rca of the issue: Stale dashboard counts after admin actions — RCA: handlers in AdminOrders.js call fetchOrders() but omit fetchSummary(); fetchSummary is only wired into the initial useEffect and the visibilityFilter dep. Reproduction: open /admin/orders, expand a paid order, click Mark Refunded — chips update to refunded/revoked/revoked, but Refunded card stays 0 and Refunds stays $0. Mitigation: add fetchSummary() call after every successful action mutation in AdminOrders.js, or extract a `refreshAll = () => { fetchOrders(); fetchSummary(); }` helper and replace all in-handler fetchOrders() calls with refreshAll().
